On Your Turn
Each turn you can Move, take one Action, maybe one Bonus Action, and between turns one Reaction.
Actions
  • Attack with a weapon or damaging cantrip (see Skills page)
  • Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Help, Search, Ready, Shove, Grapple, Influence, Study, Utilize

Reactions
  • Opportunity Attack when a creature leaves your reach

House Rules
  • Catch your breath. Out of combat, spend one Hit Die + your Constitution modifier to heal. Up to 3 times all run; mark each on the Hit Dice track above.
  • Spellcasting. Cast any spell of a type you can cast from a found Spell Book, if you have the slots. You can reach one level above your normal maximum by spending two slots of the level just below it: two level-1 slots cast a level-2 spell, two level-2 slots cast a level-3 spell like Fireball. That over-level cast needs a spellcasting check (DC 10 + the spell's level). The slots are spent whether you pass or fail, and a failure fizzles the spell.

The Vault of the Starving MindPage 3

Who You Are

Your Ancestry: Lizardfolk

Your ancestry gives you a few natural traits.

Bite. You have a fanged maw that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with it, the strike deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
Hold Breath. You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes at a time.
Hungry Jaws. You can throw yourself into a feeding frenzy. As a bonus action, you can make a special attack with your Bite. If the attack hits, it deals its normal damage, and you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
Natural Armor. You have tough, scaly skin. When you aren’t wearing armor, your base AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC.
Nature’s Intuition. Thanks to your mystical connection to nature, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.
Your Background: Criminal

You eked out a living in dark alleyways, cutting purses or burgling shops. Perhaps you were part of a small gang of like-minded wrongdoers who looked out for each other.

Trained Skills. Sleight of Hand and Stealth (already on your Skills page).
Tools. Thieves’ Tools.
Origin Feat. Alert (explained under Your Feats).
Your Feats

Feats are special perks from your background and choices, on top of your class.

Alert. Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Initiative Proficiency. When you roll Initiative, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the roll. Initiative Swap. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can swap your Initiative with the Initiative of one willing ally in the same combat.
Weapon Mastery. Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.
Dark Bargain. A pact perk from your backstory. Confirm its exact effect with your DM before play.
Character Threads. Threads are aspects added to characters at any time during their career that have a specific short or long-term goal.
Runestones. At the beginning of the Northlands Sagas adventure path, each player should draw one Runestone randomly.
Your Class: Rogue (Assassin)
The Vault of the Starving MindPage 4

Who You Are

A Dexterous Expert in Stealth and Subterfuge. Rogues have a knack for finding the solution to just about any problem, prioritizing subtle strikes over brute strength. Primary Ability: Dexterity. Hit Point Die: D8. Saves: Dexterity & Intelligence

Practice the Grim Art of Death. An Assassin’s training focuses on using stealth, poison, and disguise to eliminate foes with deadly efficiency.

Sneak Attack. Free (once per turn). Once per turn, deal an extra 2d6 damage to a creature you hit with a Finesse or Ranged weapon, if you have Advantage on the attack or if an enemy of the target is within 5 ft of it and you don't have Disadvantage.
Cunning Action. Bonus Action. On your turn, take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a Bonus Action.
Steady Aim. Bonus Action. If you haven't moved this turn, give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll this turn. Your Speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn.
Expertise. Passive. You have Expertise (double your proficiency bonus) in two skills. They are marked on your Skills page.
Weapon Mastery. Passive. You can use the mastery property of two kinds of weapons you chose.
Assassinate. Passive / Free. You have Advantage on Initiative. During the first round of combat you have Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet, and the first time you Sneak Attack such a creature that round, it takes extra damage equal to your Rogue level.
Assassin's Tools. Passive. You gain a Disguise Kit and a Poisoner's Kit and proficiency with both.
